- If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00) and forecast is trending upward, reduce slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast starts rising sharply after a recent dip, cap the initial spike to prevent overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows sudden large spikes (e.g., >10% from prior), model should adjust downward in next period to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- If history shows mean-reverting patterns (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days near 78–80), forecast should not drift beyond ±5% of recent mean.  
- If sentiment is positive (1.00) and forecast is flat, slightly increase slope to reflect bullish sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid linear extrapolation — introduce smoothing or decay factor to dampen momentum bias.  
- If true outcome deviates >15% from forecast in early days (e.g., day 1–3), reset forecast anchor to true value or recent 7-day average.  
- When sentiment is neutral and true outcome spikes, forecast should not follow until at least 2–3 days of stabilization.  
- Avoid forecasting above 90% of recent 14-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (1.00) and confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
